extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimental scientists (readers of the Royal Society)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit standards for designing, conducting, reporting, and assessing 17th‑century natural‑philosophy experiments, measurements, and claims of invention (as exemplified by pneumatical experiments, hydrological estimates, mine observations, and priority disputes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of controlled comparative experiments (vacuo vs open air)
rubrics_metrics.description: On mixing equal parts of aquafortis and aquavitas, and putting two equal quantities of the mixture in two small glasses, with two equal bits of iron, one in each, and including one of the glasses in vacuo, there was seen a very great ebullition, and the liquor became black; whilst the other glass that was left without the receiver ... remained always transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run parallel experiments that vary only the condition under test (e.g., presence/absence of vacuum). Use equal quantities and identical ancillary items (bits of iron, equal glasses) so differences in outcome (ebullition, dissolution, colour change) can be attributed to the experimental variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a gauge to detect and quantify generated air
rubrics_metrics.description: A gauge was put into the receiver, which is a glass tube, filled either with water freed of air or with mercury, 4 inches long; and it was observed, that when the liquors were mixed together, the water in the gauge rose very nimbly to the top; and then exhausting this new air, the gauge water subsided again by degrees, in like manner as when the common air is drawn out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the production and behaviour of gas with a physical gauge (water or mercury column), observe rises/falls, and perform exhaustion to confirm the gas's elasticity and behaviour relative to atmospheric air.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe temporal stability and persistence of produced airs
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been found experimentally, that the air formed by the mixture of aquafortis and copper remains always air, and always keeps up the water in the glass at that height to which it first raised it; but ... the air produced by the mixture of oil of tartar and oil of vitriol almost all vanishes of itself in 24 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess produced gases over time to distinguish permanently elastic airs from transient effluvia; record their persistence (e.g., measurements at 24 hours) as part of gas characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove ambient air (create vacuum) to reveal volatile behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiver was so well exhausted of the air, that the spirit of wine boiled up with large bubbles ... After both these liquors were well purged of air, the upper glass was sunk into the lower, so that the spirit of wine was mingled with the aquafortis; when there was yet seen a very considerable ebullition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evacuation/vacuum to eliminate external pressure and dissolved air so latent ebullitions or volatility of substances become observable; compare behaviour before and after exhaustion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for claiming invention priority: publication and practical success
rubrics_metrics.description: It is certain then, that the describer ... some years ago, caused to be actually made some watches of this kind, yet without publishing to the world a description of the same in print; but it is as certain that none of those watches succeeded, and that nothing was done since to mend the invention, and to render it useful, that we know of, until M. Huygens sent hither a letter ... acquainting us with an invention of his of very exact pocket watches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To assert priority, a discoverer should have published a description or otherwise made the invention publicly known, and ideally demonstrated successful, useful implementation; mere private or unsuccessful attempts are weak grounds for exclusive claim. Also acknowledge possibility of independent simultaneous discovery among skilled investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize measurement units and use representative averages for hydrological estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be first necessary to agree on the way of measuring these two sorts of water. Some persons say, that a cubic inch of water yields, in 24 hours running, 144 muids ... I have found that from October 1668, to October 1669, there had fallen so much of it, as amounted to the height of 18 inches 7 lines; ... Of which, taking the medium, we have 19 inches and 2- lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agree on measurement units and methods, take measurements over representative periods, compute averages (medians/means) from multiple years, and reduce all quantities to common units before comparison (e.g., reservoir capacity vs annual river discharge). Explicitly state assumptions about basin area and boundaries used in estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe and evaluate books by content coverage, applicability, and practical advice
rubrics_metrics.description: The author first describes what he means by earth; then endeavours to show the several sorts and kinds of earth, as they reside in their several beds, with the indications, by which we may discover their qualities ... In the third part he teaches ... how we may best improve it to the uses of the husbandman, the forester, and the gardener.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing technical books, summarize the structure and main parts, note methods and tools presented (e.g., microscopical examination), and assess their practical usefulness to practitioners as well as originality or rectification of prior literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify generated gases by chemical and biological assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Boyle ... mentioned also some ways of examining whether the substance thus produced be true air or not. And long before that time ... Mr. Boyle mentioned ... that corals or oyster shells pounded, and put into distilled vinegar, might prove fit substances to produce air wholesome for breathing. ... Mr. Hook made the experiment ... the bladder, tied on to the other pipe, swelled up very plump with air; which expansion remained till the Society rose, ... the bladder was then found somewhat shrunk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chemical reactions, behaviour with lime/mercury/water, and biological tests (support of respiration for animals) to determine whether a produced aeriform body is common air, fixed air (carbonic acid), nitrous gas, etc. Combine physical containment tests (bladder expansion and shrinkage) with chemical/physiological assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize and mitigate mine damps by observation and air circulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Damps are most generally observed to come about the latter end of May, and to continue during the heat of summer ... Some damps will quite extinguish all those fires that are let down into them ... they are a present remedy, if by their means a circulation of air through the infected place can be made, otherwise they do hurt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record seasonality, location, smell, density relative to air, and behaviour (e.g., ability to extinguish fires). Use circulation of fresh air as a primary mitigation; avoid practices (large fires in grooves) that create or worsen damps. Note that stagnant grooves and prior fires increase pestilential damps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control processing steps (stirring, pressing) to influence material outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some plaster of Paris was also slacked in vacuo, and the ebullition of it there appeared much more than in the open air. When it is not touched, the bubbles that issue out leave large holes in it, and then it settles very uneven; but taking care to stir it till the bubbles escape, and pressing it when it begins to settle, it becomes very smooth, and has fewer little holes than the common plaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and control handling steps (stirring, pressing, timing) during material processing to eliminate defects (large holes, uneven settling). Report such manipulations as they materially affect experimental or practical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify arithmetic and unit conversions in quantitative claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Some particulars being thus supposed, then, according to the measures agreed on, 1200 inches of water furnish in 24 hours ... 99600 muids of water; hence, in a whole year, ... they will furnish near 36-1 millions of muids. ... * There is some mistake in these numbers, as 2444- would remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check calculations and unit reductions carefully; flag and correct numerical inconsistencies in reported quantitative estimates. Explicit footnotes or editorial notes pointing out arithmetic mistakes are appropriate.
